title: pr-review-scratchpad-dataset-cache-refactor
content:
Context:
- PR: dataset cache refactor (GH #482). Goal: move dataset-level KV cache handling into DatasetCache abstraction, simplify per-model cache keys, and enable shared cache across model variants.
- Author: @maya-singh. Size: medium (12 files, lots of plumbing). Target: dedicated-serving rollout next sprint.

Quick summary of changes I saw:
- Introduced DatasetCache class (dataset_cache.py) with get/put/evict APIs.
- Replaced inline cache key construction in two places: request router and batcher.
- Moved serialization of cache entries to proto v2 (cache_entry.proto) and added versioning field.
- Added unit tests for DatasetCache (cache_test.py) but many edge cases missing.

My checklist (walked through while reading code):
- Behavior correctness:
  - [x] API surface is minimal and consistent (get/put/evict).
  - [ ] Cache key construction: ensure model variant + tokenizer settings included. Current key only includes dataset_id + request.prefix_hash. Missing quantization/profile variant.
  - [ ] Eviction semantics: LRU not implemented? The in-memory impl uses simple dict with TTL; no size-based eviction. Need either size cap or hook to distributed cache eviction policy.
  - [ ] Concurrency: DatasetCache.put is not thread-safe for shared mem implementation (no locks). Batcher uses concurrent workers -> race possible.

- Tests:
  - [x] Basic put/get tests present.
  - [ ] Missing concurrency test (multiple threads put/get).
  - [ ] No serialization compatibility test between proto v1 and v2. Migration path not documented.
  - [ ] Need test for cache-miss fallback to compute path (makes sure no double-compute).

- Performance and perf-safety:
  - [ ] DatasetCache.get is synchronous and may block batcher loop if cache backend latency spikes. Consider adding async path or time budget.
  - [ ] Proto serialize/deserialize happens on hot path; consider benchmarking CPU cost for v2 vs v1.

- Security/data handling:
  - [x] No user PII stored in cache keys. Keys are hashed prefix. Good.
  - [ ] Check that encrypted cache backend will be used for private deployments (note in PR mentions config flag but not enforced). Add integration test in private env.

- Documentation and API:
  - [ ] Add docstring on DatasetCache explaining semantics (TTL, eviction, concurrency guarantees).
  - [ ] Add note in ops runbook about cache migration when rolling to dedicated serving.

Specific code smells / refactor ideas:
- dataset_cache.py: DatasetCache has both in-memory and redis adapter implemented in same file; split adapters into adapters/ directory to keep core abstraction smaller.
- cache_entry.proto: version field is an int but treated as string in a comment; be explicit and add enum for versions to avoid accidental mismatch.
- router changes: router still constructs a pre-cache key in one legacy path (router/legacy_router.py:line ~214). There's a call path that bypasses new DatasetCache entirely for "fast-path" requests. We should either remove or add an adapter shim.
- tests/cache_test.py: lots of duplicated setup. Use pytest fixtures to share redis-mock setup.

Follow-ups and TODOs for author (@maya-singh):
- Please add model-variant info to cache key. Quick suggestion: include model_name + quantization_profile short id and hash them into key.
- Add a size-based eviction policy (configurable). If you want, I can sketch an LRU wrapper using OrderedDict with lock for in-memory.
- Add a simple concurrency test (spawn 8 threads, random put/get on same key) and assert no exceptions/duplicate compute.
- Add a migration note for proto v2: how do we handle reading v1 blobs? Add a migration util that can detect version and convert.
- Call out the fast-path that bypasses DatasetCache. Is that intentional? If so, add comment and test to ensure invariants.

Small nit picks / style:
- Use f-strings consistently in dataset_cache logging (avoid % formatting).
- Add type hints to public methods (return Optional[CacheEntry]).
- Prefer dataclass for cache entry wrappers rather than raw dicts for clarity.

Edge-case example to reproduce locally:
1) Start runtime with in-memory cache.
2) Send two concurrent requests for same prefix; one thread triggers compute and put, other tries get -> if race exists both compute.
3) Re-run with redis adapter: should only compute once.

Suggested patch outline (what I'd push if I had time):
- small: add model-variant to key + unit test (easy, ~20 LOC).
- medium: extract adapters/redis_adapter.py and inmem_adapter.py, add locks to inmem impl, add concurrency test (~150 LOC).
- follow-up: async get path and proto migration util (bigger design convo).

Notes to self (questions for sync):
- Talk with Maya about expected cache size limits per dataset. Ops wants a knob per-customer.
- Ask SRE if we should default to redis with cluster config in dedicated envs.

Bottom line:
- PR moves us forward and the abstraction is useful, but needs: key correctness (add variant), concurrency hardening for in-memory adapter, and migration/compatibility tests before merge into main.

Action items assigned:
- @maya-singh: add variant to key + note on fast-path (blocker).
- @ethan-park: draft LRU in-memory adapter and add concurrency test (optional follow-up).
- @priya-nair: add integration test against redis-mock and proto v1->v2 compatibility check.

Recent quick todo (local branch):
- create branch review/482-fix-key -> implement key change + single unit test.

----
Unresolved questions I want answered in PR description before approving:
- Why was proto version bumped now? Migration story?
- Is there an expected max cache size per dataset? Default config?
- Is the fast-path intentionally bypassing DatasetCache? If yes, explain invariant.

End of notes.

(rough, messy — notes to self while reading PR)
